messages:
kamal: quick question — if we need to shut down the new traffic-split feature in prod right now, who is allowed to do it and what exact steps should they follow? need audit trail for compliance.

sarah: anyone in the oncall rotation + eng-platform leads can flip it. but for prod-wide disable we prefer an eng-platform lead to do the action and an oncall to verify.

alex: +1. policy: single-person flips ok for critical outages, but we document reason and ticket. for non-critical changes we want a 2nd ack in the thread.

oncall-lead: procedure in short: 1) open incident ticket 2) tag eng-platform + oncall 3) run the disable action 4) paste audit id here 5) monitor for fallout.

kamal: what's the disable command? I only have dashboard access.

sarah: dashboard path: Console > Feature Flags > traffic-split > Disable for env: prod. note: UI requires SSO + 2FA and records user id automatically.

alex: CLI (if you have perms):
```
redwood-ops feature disable --name traffic-split --env prod --reason "incident: high error rate" --ticket INC-1234
```
That prints an audit id, e.g. `audit:FF-2024-000987`. Paste that back here.

kamal: perfect. does the CLI enforce TTL/rollback?

sarah: CLI supports `--auto-rollback 10m` to auto-re-enable after X minutes. but we don't recommend unless it's a safe temp mitigation. default is manual re-enable only.

maria: heads-up: disabling traffic-split will route all traffic to classic routing. downstream canaries will be bypassed. verify model pools and quotas before flipping.

kamal: good call — I'll check quotas. who should be pinged once I have the audit id?

oncall-lead: ping @sarah and @alex and add `ops-audit-bot` to the incident ticket. ops-audit-bot will ingest the audit id and attach logs to the incident automatically.

kamal: got it. quick checklist I'm about to follow: 1) create INC ticket 2) notify here + oncall 3) run CLI disable with reason/ticket 4) paste audit id 5) verify health + routing 6) escalate to eng-platform leads if regressions.

devops-bot: reminder — prod disable actions are logged to /var/logs/feature-audit.log and forwarded to Splunk under index=ops_audit.

kamal: ran the CLI, output: `audit:FF-2024-001002` — pasted into INC-1299. disabled at 1718890123. verifying now.

maria: I see traffic fall to classic pool, latency stable. looking at quotas now.

alex: thanks. if anything abnormal in 15m, escalate to oncall lead and we can revert. also leave the re-enable decision to eng-platform leads after a postmortem.

ops-audit-bot: audit recorded: id=FF-2024-001002, user=kamal, action=disable, feature=traffic-split, env=prod, ticket=INC-1299, ts=1718890123. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/ops_audit/FF-2024-001002

kamal: closing the loop — no immediate regressions after 20m. created follow-up PR to add a guardrail that prevents disabling during global maintenance windows. will request review from @alex and @sarah.

sarah: thank you — please add a short SOP snippet in the incident so auditors see the steps taken. :thumbsup:
